trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out up or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up.
I can't rule out left or up yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.

Going up would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order); going left would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes down.
Number 3 is next and right here, so the line takes it.

Going around the edge to (1,4) would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order); going left would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So the line goes right.
Number 4 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going down, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going left, the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 7; going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes around the edge to (5,3).
Number 5 is only reachable this way.
The line must go up: left is number 7, which comes later.
Number 6 is only reachable this way.
Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going left would force the line onto number 9 before its turn. So the line goes down.
Number 8 is only reachable this way.
The line must go up: around the edge to (1,1) is number 11, which comes later.
Cell (2,5) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes around the edge to (2,5).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
